overview: The Sagarmala Port Modernisation Programme is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at modernizing India's ports through port-led development, enhancing port infrastructure, improving connectivity, and promoting industrialization and coastal community development. It focuses on port modernization, new port development, port connectivity enhancement, port-linked industrialization, and coastal community development to reduce logistics costs and boost EXIM trade.
objectives: Enhance port connectivity through rail, road, inland waterways, and coastal shipping
Promote port-led industrialization and coastal economic zones
Develop coastal communities through skill development and livelihood projects
Reduce logistics cost for EXIM and domestic cargo
Improve efficiency, productivity, and competitiveness of Indian ports
Develop new major ports and upgrade existing ones
Promote inland waterways and coastal shipping as sustainable transport modes
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include major ports under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, state governments, state maritime boards, private sector entities through public-private partnerships (PPP), and other government agencies involved in port infrastructure and connectivity projects, subject to project appraisal and approval under the Sagarmala framework.
benefits: Financial assistance for project development, infrastructure creation, and connectivity enhancement; technical support for project planning and implementation; promotion of public-private partnerships; improved port efficiency and reduced vessel turnaround time; enhanced logistics infrastructure leading to lower logistics costs; development of coastal economic zones and employment generation; skill development and sustainable livelihood projects for coastal communities.
financial_support: The programme provides financial support in the form of grants, equity, and debt financing for port modernization, connectivity projects, port-linked industrialization, and coastal community development. Funding is sourced from budgetary allocations, extra-budgetary resources, and private investment through PPP models. Specific financial mechanisms include viability gap funding (VGF), interest subordination, and capital subsidies, with disbursal tied to project milestones and approvals by the Sagarmala Apex Committee and National Sagarmala Apex Committee (NSAC).
application_process: 1. Project identification by port authorities, state governments, or implementing agencies. 2. Preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) with techno-economic feasibility. 3. Submission of DPR to the Sagarmala Cell or concerned nodal agency. 4. Appraisal by the Project Appraisal Committee (PAC) or Independent Expert Body. 5. Recommendation for approval by the Sagarmala Apex Committee. 6. Final approval by the National Sagarmala Apex Committee (NSAC). 7. Signing of Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or Concession Agreement. 8. Disbursal of funds in tranches based on project progress. 9. Monitoring and evaluation by the Sagarmala Monitoring Cell.
required_documents: Environmental and social impact assessment (if applicable)
Clearances from relevant regulatory authorities (e.g., MoEFCC, customs, etc.)
Draft concessionaire agreement or MoU (for PPP projects)
Board resolution or administrative approval from sponsoring agency
Undertaking regarding compliance with statutory requirements
deadlines: Rolling basis — project proposals can be submitted throughout the year, subject to appraisal cycles and availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
caveats: Projects must align with the Sagarmala National Perspective Plan (NPP) and contribute to port-led development objectives
Financial support is contingent on project appraisal, techno-economic viability, and adherence to timelines
Private sector participation requires transparent bidding and adherence to PPP guidelines
Funding may be withdrawn or suspended for non-compliance, delays, or deviation from approved scope
Coastal community development projects require active participation of local communities and convergence with other central/state schemes
